description: Cut wheat bound at the waist, dry as paper. Somebody is still cutting a strip of that field every summer.
lore: The field grew itself, the way fields here do, out of a great many people being sure what a summer looks like. It does not need cutting. It is cut anyway, one strip a year along the north edge, by an old man with a scythe he made himself and has rehung twice. He binds at the waist, one turn and a tuck, and the collectors know his knot on sight and pay over the going rate for it, which he has never found out. Ask him why and he is perfectly clear: a field with nothing taken out of it looks wrong to him, and he would rather not look at it. He is not [[lore/the_quiet|thinning]]. People who love him have asked, kindly, and he says so, and he is very probably right. Every year the strip is in the same place.
gm_notes: Deliberately unresolved: a habit that looks like stage three and might just be a man who likes work. The knot is his signature and he does not know it is worth money.
